title: How does your skin renew itself without disappearing?
hook: The surface sheds cells; farther down, new cells enter the picture.
summary: In the epidermis, the skin’s outer layer, new cells formed at the base replace those shed at the surface.
cardText: Skin sheds surface cells and makes new ones at the base of the epidermis. This replacement renews its outer layer while it protects the body.

cardBlocks.text: Skin acts as a barrier between the body and the outside world, but its surface is not a covering that stays intact forever. Cells naturally flake off. Replacement begins at the base of the epidermis, the name of the skin’s outer layer, where new cells form to replace those being shed.

Along this route, cells accumulate a protein called keratin. In the outermost layer they are flattened, dead and filled with this material; they then flake away. Skin is maintained through this combination of production and loss. This describes renewal of the epidermis: beneath it lies the dermis, containing blood vessels and nerve endings.
In the epidermis, new cells formed at the base replace those shed at the surface.

deepDiveBlocks.text: The epidermis is not equally thick everywhere. It is thicker on the palms and soles than in many other places. That does not turn the whole skin into one layer: the dermis lies beneath the epidermis.
Along with protection from the environment, skin helps keep fluids inside the body and contributes to sensing touch and temperature. A renewing surface remains part of an organ with several jobs.
